If the mother is sensitized to the fetus' blood type, antibodies will attack the red blood cells of the fetus, causing it to undergo lysis. This creates a positive lumen potential and a negative serosal potential, which drives the electrochemical gradient for K+ and organic anions out of the enterocytes. This increases the efficiency of monosaccharide absorption. In the pancreas, the opposite occurs. CFTR facilitates diffusion of Cl- out of acinar cells, which causes water to follow by osmosis. This creates a negative lumen potential and a positive serosal potential, which drives the electrochemical gradient for K+ and organic anions out of the acinus cells. This increases the efficiency of amino acid absorption. In CF, the CFTR is dysfunctional and so Cl- cannot diffuse out of acinar cells. Water is not drawn out by osmosis and so a negative lumen potential and a positive serosal potential cannot be created. K+ and organic anions cannot be absorbed and so the pancreas cannot absorb amino acids.

NSAIDs inhibit the COX domain of PGHS, which produces prostaglandin H synthase. This inhibits the production of prostacyclin (PGI2) from the endothelium. Prostacyclin is a vasodilator and also a thromborepellant, as it inhibits platelets from aggregating. It is therefore a key factor in preventing thrombosis. The other product of COX is thromboxane (TXA2) which is a vasoconstrictor and promotes platelet aggregation. Therefore, when NSAIDs are used chronically, the balance between these two factors favours TXA2 and so the likelihood of thrombosis increases.

The statement is describing the changes that occur to cause the closure of the foramen ovale.  At birth, the first breath causes the alveoli to inflate and the arterioles to dilate. This leads to a large drop in pressure in the pulmonary system. The pressure in the right atrium is now significantly lower than in the left atrium. This causes the foramen ovale to be pushed shut. The pressure difference between the two atria is what maintains the septum primum and septum secundum apart. The foramen ovale is now closed and blood cannot pass through it. This leads to the formation of the fossa ovalis.  The ductus arteriosus closes due to the change in hormonal levels at birth. The decrease in prostaglandins causes it to close and form the ligamentum arteriosum.  The umbilical arteries close due to the action of the semilunar valves and the pressure from the umbilical vein. They form the medial umbilical ligament and inferior vesical ligament.  The ductus venosus becomes the ligamentum venosum.

First lets work out what the ABG shows:  Low O2 - he is still hypoxic  Normal pH - so is compensated  High CO2 - respiratory acidosis  High HCO3 and BE - metabolic compensation  So he has chronic respiratory acidosis with metabolic alkalosis compensation.  In chronic states, the body is able to compensate so that pH remains normal.  In acute states, there is not enough time for compensation so pH will be deranged.

Vitamin E is an antagonist of vitamin A. Excessive amounts of vitamin E can inhibit the absorption of vitamin A. Vitamin A is essential in the synthesis of rhodopsin. Rhodopsin is essential for low light vision. A lack of vitamin A will inhibit the synthesis of rhodopsin and so night vision will be impaired.
